direction.comments: The direction on a macroscale feels like a 2000s feel-good movie, which is Anne Hathaway's bread and butter; The direction on a microscale is very 2000s feel-good, but it helps highlight Andy's struggle trying to fit in as a new graduate; The storytelling is quite 2000s; The tension is very 2000s

performance.comments: Embodies Anna Wintour's persona as she creates a character that is both terrifying and powerful; has good chemistry with the cast and makes her scenes memorable

The real heart for the movie because I love his character's dynamic with Anne Hathaway's as he acts as a mentor figure to her and is the only one who truly sees her potential, despite also being stern

I don't understand why everyone hates this dude, I think he's basically doing what any guy in that situation would do

cast.comments: The supporting cast is just your typical feel-good 2000s ensemble; chemistry is decent

story.comments: The concept is iconic, as it takes us into the 2000s fashion world with Runway and Miranda being fictionalized versions of Vogue and Anna Wintour, and it follows an optimistic journalist navigating this world as she tries to fit in, grow her career, and come to terms with the impostor syndrome she faces as a new graduate; The plot structure is quite simple and exactly what you would expect from a 2000s feel-good comedy; The character writing is surprisingly good, because even though this is a very surface-level movie, the characters actually have some nuance that makes them ultimately iconic; The characters represent the following: Meryl Streep is a fictionalized version of Anna Wintour who is both terrifying yet iconic, Anne Hathaway's character is an allegory for the journey of a new graduate, Emily Blunt's character is the perfect foil to Anne Hathaway's because she is career-obsessed from a fashion perspective, and Stanley Tucci's character is the heart of the movie, acting as a mentor figure to Anne Hathaway's character and being the only one who sees her potential

screenplay.comments: The dialogue is quite simple and exactly what you would expect from a 2000s feel-good comedy; The humor is quite good and makes the movie fun to watch; The symbolism is simple yet palatable, as this movie acts as an allegory for the new graduate experience; The foreshadowing is quite straightforward and makes the movie predictable

score.comments: The score feels like it belongs in a 2000s feel-good comedy, but it is so poorly mixed that it is loud enough that you can barely hear what anyone is saying

soundtrack.comments: The soundtrack helps make this movie feel very much targeted toward girls during the 2000s

cinematography.comments: The cinematography is very 2000s, as it feels like a 2000s feel-good comedy, especially those that star Anne Hathaway

editing.comments: The editing employs some cool techniques, especially during the dress montages, but it also feels very 2000s on a macroscale

sound.comments: The sound mixing for this movie was atrocious, as you can barely hear what anyone is saying with the score and soundtrack blasting throughout the movie

visual_effects.comments: There is only one VFX shot in this movie and it is bad, because it is very obvious that they are in a car that is fake driving with a green screen behind them

production_design.comments: The production design showcases the 2000s fashion world well in both New York and Paris

makeup.comments: The makeup helps paint these characters as fashion icons, but it feels very much like a 2000s feel-good comedy

costumes.comments: It feels customary for the costumes to be the highlight of this movie because the film is all about the fashion world, but they help make this movie iconic and build the world that Runway creates

review.pacing: The pacing is just right, as it does not feel too slow or too fast
review.climax: The climax is pretty formulaic for a 2000s feel-good comedy, but it ends the movie on an optimistic note that makes you root for the characters
review.tone: The tone is incredibly like a 2000s feel-good comedy, as this movie feels like the peak of the 2000s Anne Hathaway era
review.overall: Overall, 'The Devil Wears Prada' is incredibly '2000s feel-good' in its tone and storytelling, as it feels like the peak of the 2000s Anne Hathaway era, but it is still iconic and fun to watch; even though the symbolism feels simple and overt, this helps make the movie more palatable, as the film is actually a surprisingly accurate allegorical tale of the new graduate experience
